claim.quote: We observed the oscillation effect at CL $3.5\sigma$ in the vicinity of $\Delta m^2_{14} \approx 7.26\textrm{eV}^2$ and $\sin^2 2\theta_{14} \approx 0.38$.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published JETP Letters 109, 213 (2019).

key_value_text.quote: We observed the oscillation effect at CL $3.5\sigma$ in the vicinity of $\Delta m^2_{14} \approx 7.26\textrm{eV}^2$ and $\sin^2 2\theta_{14} \approx 0.38$.
key_value_text.value: Oscillation effect at CL 3.5 sigma near delta m^2_14 ~ 7.26 eV^2 and sin^2(2 theta_14) ~ 0.38

name: The first observation of effect of oscillation in Neutrino-4 experiment on search for sterile neutrino
notes: Disfavoured by PROSPECT (arXiv:2406.10408), whose abstract says the Neutrino-4 best-fit point is ruled out at more than five standard deviations.

significance.quote: We observed the oscillation effect at CL $3.5\sigma$

summary.plain: The Neutrino-4 team reported that the antineutrino rate at its different distances from the reactor oscillates in a way a sterile neutrino would cause, at about 3.5 standard deviations. This is a claimed hint, short of discovery level, and later experiments did not confirm it.
summary.technical: Model-independent coherent addition of measurements over 6-12 m: oscillation effect at 3.5 sigma near delta m^2_14 ~ 7.26 eV^2, sin^2(2 theta_14) ~ 0.38; combined with the gallium anomaly sin^2(2 theta_14) ~ 0.35 +- 0.07 (5 sigma).

title: The first observation of effect of oscillation in Neutrino-4 experiment on search for sterile neutrino
why_it_matters: The only reactor-experiment claim of a sterile-neutrino signal; it motivated the PROSPECT, STEREO, DANSS and other tests.
